candidates.exact_span: toxicity tests conducted on effluent discharges where no receiving water is available due to zero flow conditions.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether zero-flow conditions exist and whether receiving water is 'unavailable' determines whether effluent-only toxicity testing substitutes for receiving-water testing, changing which monitoring obligations apply (B) and how missing or alternate-result cases are classified when normal receiving-water monitoring cannot occur (C).

candidates.exact_span: If the receiving water is unsatisfactory as a result of instream toxicity (fails to fulfill the test acceptance criteria), the permittee may substitute synthetic dilution water for the receiving water in all subsequent tests provided the unacceptable receiving water test met the following stipulations:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of when receiving water is 'unsatisfactory' or fails acceptance criteria, and whether substitution is permitted versus required, changes which subsequent toxicity monitoring pathway applies (B) and whether reported results reflect required or optional alternative procedures (C).

candidates.exact_span: a synthetic dilution water control which fulfills the test acceptance requirements was run concurrently with the receiving water control;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this concurrent-control condition was satisfied affects whether synthetic dilution water may be used in subsequent tests, altering applicable monitoring requirements (B) and whether results obtained under substitution are valid evidence or leave applicability unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: the test indicating receiving water toxicity has been carried out to completion,
candidates.computation_change_reason: What counts as a toxicity test 'carried out to completion' determines whether the permittee qualifies to switch to synthetic dilution water, changing which monitoring obligations govern later tests (B) and how incomplete or partial test evidence is classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: the permittee includes all test results indicating receiving water toxicity with the full report and information required;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether all required toxic receiving-water results and reporting were included affects eligibility for synthetic dilution water substitution, changing applicable monitoring duties (B) and whether missing reports represent documented no-data, inadequate evidence, or unresolved cases (C).

candidates.exact_span: the synthetic dilution water shall have a pH, hardness, and alkalinity similar to that of the receiving water or closest downstream perennial water not adversely affected by the discharge, provided the magnitude of these parameters will not cause toxicity in the synthetic dilution water.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'similar' parameters, which reference water applies when the receiving water is unsatisfactory, and whether synthetic water itself caused toxicity affects whether substituted toxicity results are valid for numeric limit comparison (A) and whether the substituted monitoring pathway was properly followed (B).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall collect two samples (flow-weighted composite if possible) from the outfall(s).
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes a mandatory two-sample collection obligation and whether flow-weighted compositing is required when possible; different readings of 'if possible' or which outfall(s) are covered change which sampling requirements were applicable.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall collect a second sample (composite samples if possible) for use during the 24-hour renewal of each dilution concentration for each test.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a separate second sample is required for each dilution renewal during toxicity testing, and when compositing is required, changes the count and timing of applicable monitoring obligations for each test event.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must collect the composite samples so that the maximum holding time for any effluent sample shall not exceed 36 hours for first use of the sample. The permittee must have initiated the toxicity test within 36 hours after the collection of the last portion of the first composite sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of holding-time limits and when the 'first use' or test initiation clock starts affects whether collected samples and resulting measurements are valid for numeric compliance comparison (A), whether sampling procedures were required and satisfied (B), and whether late or missing initiation is documented noncompliance, excused delay, or unresolved evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: A holding time up to 72 hrs is allowed upon notification to EPA and NMED of the need for additional holding time.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether notification occurred and additional holding time was authorized changes whether samples beyond 36 hours remain valid for limit comparison (A), whether extended holding was an allowed monitoring condition (B), and whether absence of results reflects an approved extension versus inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Samples shall be chilled to 6 degrees Centigrade during collection, shipping, and/or storage.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether chilling to 6°C was required and achieved affects the validity of toxicity measurements for numeric limit comparison (A) and whether sampling and handling obligations were met (B).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must collect the composite samples such that the effluent samples are representative of the discharge duration, and of any periodic episode of chlorination, biocide usage or other potentially toxic substance discharged on an intermittent basis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of what makes a sample 'representative' of discharge duration and intermittent toxic episodes determines when monitoring must capture episodic discharges (B), whether missing episodic coverage is conditional non-requirement or inadequate evidence (C), and which discharge events reported measurements may be compared against applicable toxicity limits (A).
